subject: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@pilotcloud.io>, support@eastern-retail.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback

Team / Tim,

We ran the preflight tests last night against the Stage cluster and want to propose a phased patch sprint for Eastern Retail's private VPC (codename: 'Surgeon'). Goal: apply the OS/network patches and the 23.3 runtime security backports with minimal customer impact and a deterministic fallback path if KV cache state becomes inconsistent.

High-level proposal (details in attached matrix):
- Phase A (drain + apply kernel & netplan changes) — 3h window, rolling across AZs, affinity to standby nodes
- Phase B (runtime security backports) — 2h window, node-by-node, zero-downtime by traffic drain and warm-cache rehydration
- Phase C (verification & extended telemetry) — 1.5h window, smoke tests and synthetic workloads

Rollforward triggers: 95% of canary queries <150ms and no elevation of error counts above baseline.
Rollback strategy: automated circuit-break to compatible 22.x runtime + rehydrate KV cache from snapshot; manual failover play for cross-AZ traffic if needed. See surgeon_rollback_playbook.md attached.

Questions for Eastern Retail / PilotCloud:
1) Any blackout windows we must avoid for retail promotion cadence?
2) Are there any IP allowlist constraints in prod load balancers we should be aware of?
3) Can PilotCloud run the netplan diff in a staging sim to validate neighbor routes?

Requested action: confirm preferred maintenance date (we're tentatively looking at Nov 17–18 UTC nights) and any constraints.

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
(Attachment: surgeon_patch_matrix.xlsx, surgeon_rollback_playbook.md)

From: Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@pilotcloud.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, support@eastern-retail.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback

Soojin — thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers from PilotCloud side:
- We can run the netplan diff simulation in staging and validate overlay routes/peerings — I can deliver a short report by EOD Wed.
- Eastern Retail has a blackout around their morning sync (Wed night UTC) — avoid 02:00–04:00 UTC on Tue/Wed of the week.
- We will need to sign off on the rollback snapshot retention (we typically keep 72h by default; you requested 7 days) — ops can extend that for this event if you confirm.

A couple of request items:
- Include a short pre-provision step in Phase A to ensure standby nodes have the expected nvme firmware (we had one mismatch last month).
- Can you provide the exact netplan change snippet so we can run through the automation runbook?

I'll loop in the staging engineer once you share the diff.

Cheers,
Tim
Tim Bryant
Principal Cloud Engineer, PilotCloud Professional Services
tim.bryant@pilotcloud.io
(Attachment: none)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback

FYI — I ran the risk checklist against the matrix and added an entry for customer-facing cache anomalies. Recommendations:
- Expand observability retention to 72h (metrics/traces) for the post-patch verification window.
- Force synthetic load that hits tail-latency sensitive paths during Phase B canary to surface regressions.
- Prepare a fast rollback stub: an infra-only switch in the service mesh to direct traffic to a 22.x pool (avoids changing DNS).

I've attached a short playbook fragment and flagged the changes in surgeon_patch_matrix.xlsx under column 'ops-risk'.

— Monica
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
(Attachment: surgeon_patch_matrix.xlsx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Tim Bryant <tim.bryant@pilotcloud.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback

Decision and next steps:
1) Confirmed maintenance window: Nov 18, 00:00–06:00 UTC (Phase A start 00:00) — respects Eastern Retail blackout (no overlap with morning sync).
2) PilotCloud to run netplan diff sim and deliver report by Nov 11 EOD.
3) Snapshot retention extended to 7 days for this event (Ops approved).
4) Jonas to own the mesh switch rollback stub; Monica to own telemetry retention & synthetic-run.
5) Soojin to circulate final side-by-side playbook and add the nvme firmware check to Phase A preflight.

Tim — please confirm you can run the staging run and that the firmware check is doable.

Thanks,
— Aditya
Senior PM, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
(Attachment: netplan_change.diff)

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC 'Surgeon' patch sprint — phased windows and zero-downtime fallback

Aditya / team — confirmed. We can run the netplan diff sim and validate NVMe firmware in staging; report will be in the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SurgeonPlaybooks) by COB Nov 11 UTC. Snapshot retention extended to 7 days is possible from our side.

We'll schedule the staging run tomorrow and ping when results are available. Looking forward to the final playbook.

— Tim
